survive the scratchpad. `wanted` is what an agent would have researched

r1-batch-a.notes: Researched under this session's tool constraints: the shared WebSearch budget for the session was already exhausted (200/200) before this batch began, so all research after the first few calls relied on WebFetch against company newsroom pages, PR Newswire/company-hosted press releases, Wikipedia, and TechCrunch tag/site-search pages (techcrunch.com/tag/<slug>/ and techcrunch.com/?s=<query> both worked well as a search substitute; Bing, Google, DuckDuckGo, Marginalia, and web.archive.org were all inaccessible or bot-blocked via WebFetch in this environment). This means funding-round coverage is uneven: Devoted Health, DispatchHealth, Hinge Health, Innovaccer, and Omada Health have multi-round histories with named investors; Aledade, Main Street Health, and Thyme Care have only their most recent (best-covered) round; Livongo has only one 2017 round plus the Teladoc acquisition. No Series A-C for Aledade could be sourced at all. All 10 assigned companies were researched and written (none skipped as out-of-scope) — all are confirmed US-headquartered operating companies. Every funding figure and investor name in this file traces to a URL actually fetched in this session; nothing was filled in from unverified background knowledge.

r1-batch-b.notes: WebSearch tool was exhausted session-wide (200/200) before this batch started, and the Brave Search proxy via WebFetch was rate-limited after light use; Yahoo Search (search.yahoo.com) via WebFetch was the most reliable substitute and was used for the bulk of this research, supplemented by direct WebFetch of company newsrooms, PR Newswire/Business Wire releases, TechCrunch/Fierce Healthcare/Forbes/Fortune articles, and Wikipedia. All 10 assigned companies were researched and written; none were skipped. Investor round-attribution for a handful of entries (e.g., Cityblock's Series A/B 'existing investor' overlaps, Hims & Hers' unlabeled Series B) relies on the cited article's own phrasing rather than a dedicated primary press release for that specific round, since standalone primary sources for every single early round were not always locatable. All amounts, dates, and investor names are backed by at least one fetched source; anything I could not corroborate (e.g., Oscar Health's 2013 seed round, an Oscar IPO total-proceeds figure, Maven's Series F valuation) was left out rather than guessed.

r1-batch-c.notes: All 9 assigned companies were researched and written. WebSearch tool budget was exhausted session-wide before this agent could use it (shared 200/200 quota consumed by other concurrent agents), so all research relied on WebFetch: direct company/press-release URLs (PR Newswire per-company archive pages worked well for Monogram Health, Pearl Health, CareBridge, Lyra Health, Grand Rounds), Google News RSS search (news.google.com/rss/search) to discover article titles/sources, marginalia-search.com and Bing News (www.bing.com/news/search) as fallback search engines once Google/DuckDuckGo/Yandex/Startpage returned CAPTCHAs and direct Google/Bing web search returned locale-mismatched junk. No companies were skipped; all 9 are US-headquartered operating companies confirmed via primary company sites.

r1-us-clinical-ai.notes: 32 US-headquartered clinical-AI companies researched, spanning: ambient documentation/scribes (Abridge, Ambience Healthcare, Suki AI, Freed, DeepScribe), clinical decision support/medical search (OpenEvidence, Regard, Glass Health, KelaHealth), medical coding/RCM/prior-auth (Iodine Software, CodaMetrix, Codoxo, AKASA, Anterior, Cohere Health, RapidClaims, Fathom, Carta Healthcare), AI nursing/patient-facing agents (Hippocratic AI, Infinitus Systems, Memora Health, Assort Health, Aiva Health), health-system-facing genAI platforms/governance (Qualified Health, Commure, Innovaccer, Truveta, Xealth, Epic Systems), and clinical-trial-matching AI (Triomics, H1, Massive Bio). Qualified Health, Truveta, and Epic Systems specifically address the 'governance' and 'notable non-VC' angles requested in the brief — Epic never raised institutional VC and Truveta is jointly owned by 17 US health systems rather than a conventional VC-backed startup. Iodine Software (acquired by Waystar, Oct 2025), Memora Health (acquired by Commure, Dec 2024), and Xealth (acquired by Samsung, 2025) are marked status=acquired but retained since they operated as independent VC-backed clinical-AI companies for most of their life and their acquirers are directly relevant to the investor graph. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON SOURCING METHOD: this session's WebSearch tool was already at its budget cap (200/200, exhausted by other agents in the same shared session) before I could issue a single query, and direct WebFetch of Google's search UI (google.com), Bing, and DuckDuckGo returned CAPTCHA/garbage pages. I worked around this by (1) fetching each company's own website directly (highest confidence, used for 'what', HQ, founders where available) and (2) fetching Google News RSS *search* URLs (news.google.com/rss/search?q=...), which reliably returned real aggregated article titles/dates/publishers/snippets even though the tool could not follow through to render most individual publisher pages (Google News redirect links mostly returned empty JS shells). Every funding figure in this file is backed by at least one such source and, where possible, a verbatim article headline as the quote. Numbers that could not be corroborated by a clear title/snippet (e.g., a Cohere Health '$450M round with Nvidia and Salesforce', a Xealth '2.7 trillion won' Samsung deal value) were deliberately dropped rather than guessed — see individual verification_notes. Investor round-attribution for Qualified Health's 9 named backers, and Truveta's 17 health-system co-owners, could not be resolved to individual named entities per round from available coverage; recorded as best-effort collective/unattributed entries with notes flagging the limitation. HQ city and founding year are missing (nulled/omitted, never guessed) for a number of companies (Abridge, Suki, DeepScribe, OpenEvidence, Commure, Iodine Software, Akasa, Cohere Health's Boston-vs-Portsmouth discrepancy, Infinitus, Assort Health, Innovaccer, Truveta's founding year, H1, Massive Bio, Carta Healthcare, Aiva Health, Fathom, KelaHealth, Glass Health) because no fetched source stated them explicitly, even though several are common industry knowledge — flagging for a future pass with working web search. Skipped: Waystar (the acquirer, not an operating clinical-AI company in this slice's scope; its acquisition of Iodine Software is recorded on that record instead). Considered but excluded from the final 32 due to time/budget: Nym Health, Akili Interactive, Viz.ai, Aidoc, and Tempus AI (the latter two lean more toward imaging/genomics AI than the clinical-workflow/LLM focus of this brief). --- ROUND 2 ADDENDUM (still 2026-08-16) --- This slice's second pass ran under an explicit WebSearch-only-exhausted constraint from the team lead: the session's WebSearch tool was already at 200/200 before I could issue a query, and the team lead confirmed it could not be raised, so this round used WebFetch exclusively — no search calls were made at all in round 2. Method: (1) direct company-site fetches (`/`, `/about`, `/portfolio`), (2) VC/CVC portfolio pages fetched by URL guess from the investor-roster.tsv name list (Oak HC/FT, General Catalyst, Town Hall Ventures, Optum Ventures worked; Flare Capital Partners and CVS Health Ventures 404'd), (3) Google News RSS search URLs (news.google.com/rss/search?q=...) — a WebFetch call, not WebSearch, so unaffected by the budget cap — which continued to reliably return real aggregated headlines/dates/publishers, and (4) Wikipedia, which resolved founding-year/founder/HQ gaps for Innovaccer, Truveta, and Epic Systems but 404'd for Abridge and Commure (no article at the guessed URL). Portfolio-page fetching was the most productive technique per the team lead's suggestion: Oak HC/FT's page surfaced Syllable, Town Hall Ventures' page surfaced Machinify, and Optum Ventures' page surfaced Humata Health — all three added as new records with the portfolio page itself as a source for the investor edge. SmarterDx and Cofactor AI were added from the team lead's named URL list and a Google News RSS lookup respectively. Investor names for Abridge, Ambience Healthcare, Infinitus Systems (Andreessen Horowitz -> a16z Bio + Health), Abridge again (CVS Health -> CVS Health Ventures, Mayo Clinic -> Mayo Clinic Ventures), and Iodine Software (Silversmith Management -> Silversmith Capital Partners) were corrected to match investor-roster.tsv's exact name_en spelling so the link resolver in build_companies.py finds a unique match instead of silently failing to link. Truveta's investor list was upgraded from a single generic '17 U.S. health systems' placeholder to 14 individually named founding/participating health systems per Wikipedia. Companies I know exist in this space but could NOT source well enough to include this round are listed in the top-level `wanted` array — notably Nabla (ambiguous whether its Brooklyn, NY office is now the actual HQ or just a US office of a Paris-headquartered company, which matters under this project's US-HQ-only rule; needs a working search to resolve), Akili Interactive, Viz.ai, Aidoc, and Tempus AI (all considered but left out as more imaging/DTx/genomics-leaning than core clinical-workflow LLM, consistent with round 1's reasoning), plus several General Catalyst / Oak HC/FT portfolio names (Notable Health, Akido, Galileo Health, Thesis Care, Adonis) that looked plausibly in-scope from their one-line portfolio descriptions but that I did not have time to independently verify and source this round. Total company count after this round: 37 (32 from round 1 + 5 new: SmarterDx, Syllable, Machinify, Humata Health, Cofactor AI).

r1-us-consumer-health.notes: IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: this slice ran almost entirely WITHOUT WebSearch. The session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200, shared across all parallel research agents) before I made a single call, and team-lead later confirmed it could not be raised. Per team-lead's follow-up instruction, I switched to WebFetch-only research using URL construction rather than search: Wikipedia articles/searches, direct company-site fetches (home/about/press/newsroom paths), and — most productively — investor portfolio pages (Forerunner Ventures, Rock Health Capital, General Catalyst) read directly for their listed portfolio-company names, which is how Omada Health, Virta Health, Prenuvo, Curology, Oula, Evidation Health and Neurotrack were added in this round. SEC EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar) was attempted for Form D filings on several private companies (Twentyeight Health, Hey Jane) but consistently returned HTTP 403 via WebFetch and had to be abandoned as a source path. This produced strong, well-sourced records with named investors for most PUBLIC or well-known VC-scale companies (Hims & Hers, GoodRx, Amwell, Teladoc, Talkspace, 23andMe, Fitbit, Ro, AliveCor, Cerebral, Bicycle Health, Spring Health, Function Health, Hinge Health, LifeStance Health, Whoop, Materna Medical, Evvy, Everly Health, Omada Health, Virta Health, Prenuvo, Curology, Oula, Evidation Health, Neurotrack), but left many private DTC consumer-health startups with only a company-site-sourced description and no funding/investor data, because their own homepages rarely list funding history and press coverage was unreachable without search. Companies I know exist and considered for this slice but could NOT source at all this session, so they are NOT in the companies array (see the 'wanted' list above for the full detail on each): Brightline, Teal Health, Included Health, Superpower, Bonafide Health. Also removed Oura from this file per team-lead's explicit correction that it is Finnish-headquartered and belongs to a later European round, not this US slice. Category coverage achieved: DTC/telehealth prescribing (Hims&Hers, Ro, Alto, Cerebral, Bicycle Health, FOLX, Twentyeight Health, Hey Jane, Curology), preventive screening/whole-body diagnostics (Function Health, Everly Health/Everlywell, Fountain Life, Proov, Evvy, Prenuvo), longevity (Fountain Life, Neurotrack), mental & behavioral health (Spring Health, Talkspace, LifeStance Health, NOCD, Cerebral, Big Health, Bicycle Health, Charlie Health), women's health across fertility/maternity/menopause (Maven Clinic, Materna Medical, Axena Health, May Health, Cofertility, Twentyeight Health, Hey Jane, Evvy, Oula), sleep/nutrition/GLP-1/metabolic (Noom, Levels Health, Virta Health, Omada Health), wearables/consumer biosensing (Whoop, Fitbit, AliveCor, Owlet, Willow Innovations, Evidation Health), and pediatric (Owlet, Charlie Health). Men's health is thin (only Ro/Hims&Hers as multi-category players; no standalone men's-health entry sourced). Delivered 44 companies total, all with a real fetched source per record; 25 of 44 carry >=1 named investor.

r1-us-health-data.notes:
SESSION RAN WITHOUT WEBSEARCH. The shared WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200, used by other teammates) before I made a single search call, and stayed exhausted for the rest of the session — team-lead confirmed it could not be raised. All research after that point used WebFetch only: company homepages/about/press pages, Wikipedia, and — the most productive channel by far — investor portfolio pages (Flare Capital, LRVHealth, .406 Ventures, Oak HC/FT, Town Hall Ventures, Optum Ventures, F-Prime Capital, Kaiser Permanente Ventures, Rock Health Capital), read off investor-roster.tsv, which yielded real investor-authored company->investor edges even where the company's own site was unreachable (404/DNS failure/403 on nearly every guessed path). SEC EDGAR and Crunchbase were tried and blocked (403) every time; two blind search-engine-via-WebFetch attempts (DuckDuckGo, Bing) were also tried and failed (CAPTCHA / irrelevant localized results) before this approach was abandoned in favor of direct URL construction.

Result: 70 companies, all schema-valid (validated against schema/company.schema.json with jsonschema.Draft202012Validator — zero errors) and against taxonomy.json's controlled vocabularies. 44 of the 70 carry >=1 named investor with a real fetched source (up from 10 before the investor-portfolio-page pass); 55 carry a funding block of some kind. Roughly 20 of the 70 are still thin (confidence 'low': a one-line description plus one investor-page or company-site source, no founding year/HQ/funding amount) — each says exactly what's missing in its own verification_notes rather than guessing. A handful of records also surface unresolved discrepancies between sources rather than silently picking one (e.g. GetWell Network: LRVHealth says 'acquired by Welsh Carson', the company's own site says 'part of SAIGroup'; Capital Rx vs. 'Judi Health (Formerly Capital Rx)' per F-Prime Capital's portfolio page vs. the company's own current site still branded Capital Rx).

Companies I know exist and would have researched with a working search, but could not source enough for a full record (or at all) this session, are listed in the top-level 'wanted' array — that's the worklist for a later round. It includes both companies never reached at all (Verato, Qventus, Rhyme, Zelis, HealthEdge, Evolent Health, Availity, Surescripts, Hospital IQ, Cardinal Analytx Solutions, NexHealth, Rightway, Iodine Software, Ribbon Health, Talix, Ingenious Med, ClosedLoop, Shyft) and existing thin records that need a follow-up pass to fill in founding year/HQ/funding amounts/investor names (most of the LRVHealth-alumni-sourced acquisitions, several Oak HC/FT and Optum Ventures portfolio companies, Waystar, Health Catalyst, Turquoise Health, and others — see 'wanted' for the full list with specifics).

r2-investor-gaps.notes: WebSearch was unavailable this session (budget exhausted); all research used WebFetch only. Cross-referencing the 189-name worklist against this repo's own data/companies/_raw/*.json (130 already-researched US company records) found that every single name in the worklist traces back to a funding-round investor list already present in this codebase — this is how sourcing was anchored for most records (reusing peer agents' already-verified press-release/Wikipedia quotes as valid provenance), supplemented with fresh WebFetch of each investor's own site/Wikipedia page where reachable. Many official investor sites, SEC EDGAR, Crunchbase, Bing and DuckDuckGo were blocked or returned no usable content (403/404/CAPTCHA/empty) for a large share of attempted lookups; those cases are called out explicitly in each record's verification_notes or in the corresponding rejected[] reason. A major structural finding: 19 of the 189 names (Tenet Healthcare, Advocate Aurora Health, AdventHealth, Baptist Health, Bon Secours Mercy Health, Hawaii Pacific Health, HealthPartners, Henry Ford Health, HonorHealth, Inova, MedStar Health, Novant Health, Ochsner Health, Sanford Health, Sentara Healthcare, Texas Health Resources, TriHealth, Virtua Health, WellSpan Health) plus 'Illumina' and the aggregate row '17 U.S. health systems (collective founding owners)' all trace to a single source: truveta.com/members, the health-data collaborative Truveta. These are co-ownership stakes in one joint venture, not a repeat venture-investing track record, so all were rejected under the 'not one incidental deal' rule — except Memorial Hermann, Trinity Health, and UnityPoint Health(Ventures), which the task brief had already confirmed as real and which also showed multi-company investing patterns beyond Truveta membership in this repo's own company data, so those three were included. r2-us-techbio.notes: This slice was researched WebFetch-only (no WebSearch budget). Coverage was heavily constrained by two recurring failure modes: (1) many corporate sites are JS-rendered SPAs whose blog/news/press listings return no usable content to the fetcher even at 200 status, and (2) Wikipedia article titles had to be guessed and many newer/private AI-drug-discovery startups have no article at all. Public companies were the highest-yield category because stockanalysis.com and Wikipedia both reliably surface founding, HQ, IPO and ticker data server-side. As a result the 30 delivered companies skew toward already-public techbio/tools names (20 of 30) plus 10 private companies, several of which (Xaira, Paige, Dyno, Glyphic, Terray-class names) are recorded with 'low'/'medium' confidence and no funding block because their own sites would not yield financial detail to WebFetch. SEC EDGAR (cgi-bin/browse-edgar) returned HTTP 403 on every attempt, so no S-1/10-K data was used. Investor-syndicate depth is uneven: Solugen, Enveda, Resilience, BigHat Biosciences and Tempus AI carry multi-investor lists; several public companies (10x Genomics, Twist Bioscience, Codexis, Charles River, Certara, Veracyte, Natera, Personalis, Standard BioTools, Absci, Nautilus, Quantum-Si) carry an IPO/ticker record but no named pre-IPO VCs because that detail sits behind sources (Crunchbase, PitchBook, SEC S-1) that 403'd or weren't guessable this session.
